title: A chronological experiment with nested validation
subtitle: Primary horizon: next calendar month; common target sample for all eligible models
caption: The first 84 completed monthly targets train the January 2023 forecast. Inner validation is inside that training history; every later outer origin expands the history and refits. Annual retuning reuses only preceding validation targets. The independent unit is the month, not each company-month row.

title: After the extraction repairs, most candidates are usable for most issuers
subtitle: Origin rows December 2015-August 2026 - descriptive availability, left, and the share clearing the training gate, right
caption: The left panel averages nonmissing share within each group; the right shows the share of candidates in that group whose coverage clears the 70% training-only gate, which is what determines whether a variable can enter a fit. The right panel is the operative one: a group can average high availability while individual variables fail, as the high-yield credit spread does from a 2023 archive start and interest coverage does for Materion and ATI. Three extraction defects were repaired during this continuation - Entegris equity, Carpenter trailing earnings and Materion free cash flow - and the coverage shown here is after those repairs.

title: More elaborate return models rarely improve the benchmark
subtitle: 44 one-month targets per company • January 2023–August 2026
caption: Models use the same forecast dates and historical-mean denominator. The historical mean is the denominator, so its own bar is exactly zero by construction and none is drawn. Negative R² means larger squared errors than the origin-available mean. Identical axes preserve cross-company comparability; the full tables also report MAE, direction and correlation.

title: Adding information in the protocol order changes little out of sample
subtitle: Historical mean → financial → valuation → changes/lags → market → industry → business drivers • 44 matched target months
caption: Company colours are shared by both panels and shown once, in the left legend. The left panel scores each cumulative stage against its own origin-available historical mean; the right shows the paired month-by-month loss change relative to the immediately preceding stage, with 95% moving-block intervals. A missing interval means the matched pair was ineligible. This ordering does not uniquely allocate information shared between blocks, which is why the market-first ladder and the leave-one-block-out checks are reported beside it.

title: MTRN forecasts explain little of its monthly swings
subtitle: Out-of-sample targets January 2023–August 2026 • horizon one month
caption: Black is realized adjusted-close return; all other lines were generated at the preceding month’s final close. The pooled booster is displayed as a tested comparison, not a prospectively selected winner. Forecast intervals are not estimated.

title: Incremental factors have different effects across issuers
subtitle: Historical mean → market → financial → valuation → momentum → risk → industry → business → dynamics → interactions
caption: Each row refits and retunes the cumulative Ridge specification on the same 44 target months. Improvements between rows are order-dependent. Full-minus-block checks provide a second view; zero or unchanged results can also arise when the added factor fails coverage.

title: Differences and lags are separate empirical questions
subtitle: 44 monthly tests • 95% pointwise moving-block intervals, six-month blocks
caption: P/E representations are compared with P/E level; financial changes and all-core lag models are compared with Compact Ridge. Intervals condition on saved forecasts and are not adjusted for model search. Zero ATI/CRS P/E contrasts reflect excluded sparse P/E inputs, not economic equivalence.

title: Random Forest importance does not identify causal drivers
subtitle: Return forecasts • 20 group permutations in three-month blocks across 44 target origins
caption: Positive values indicate worse error when the group is disturbed. Bars are one permutation standard deviation, not confidence intervals. Saved origin-specific models stay fixed; shuffling can break cross-group dependence, so this retrospective diagnostic is interpreted alongside controlled ablations.

title: Any advantage arrives in a few months, not steadily
subtitle: Cumulative paired squared-error difference for the four prespecified contrasts • January 2023–August 2026
caption: Each line accumulates the reduced model’s squared error minus the expanded model’s, so a rising line favours the expanded model. A step change identifies a single influential month rather than a persistent edge; a flat line means the two models effectively agreed. Panels use issuer-specific vertical scales because the magnitudes differ by an order of magnitude, so heights must not be compared across panels — only shapes. Lines stop where matched forecasts are unavailable and are not connected across gaps.

title: Residual dependence alone does not establish a forecast advantage
subtitle: MTRN • 44 saved one-month forecast errors, January 2023–August 2026
caption: The left panel shows forecast misses; the right shows lag-1 through lag-6 error autocorrelation. This is a post-evaluation diagnostic, not another tuning opportunity. No IID confidence bands are imposed on the short, adaptively fitted error sequence.

title: Model rankings can change as the evaluation window moves
subtitle: MTRN • 12-target-month rolling errors • December 2023–August 2026
caption: Every point uses the latest 12 already realized out-of-sample targets; lower values are better. Windows overlap and must not be counted as independent evidence. Return and variance panels use different loss functions with explicit units.

title: Longer-horizon results are a sensitivity, not independent confirmation
subtitle: One month: 44 targets, Jan 2023–Aug 2026 • three months: 38 overlapping targets ending Jul 2023–Aug 2026
caption: Each horizon uses its own matured historical-mean benchmark. The three-month fits purge unmatured labels and use a later start; R² changes therefore mix horizon and period effects. All three nonoverlapping offsets, only 12–13 outcomes each, are archived.

title: Compact return slopes vary by company and refit
subtitle: Median and interquartile range across 44 expanding-window OLS fits
caption: Dots show median coefficients measured per training standard deviation; whiskers show across-origin interquartile ranges, not sampling confidence intervals. Unavailable predictors produce blank entries. Scaling makes within-model effects readable, but differs between companies and dates; raw slopes are also archived.

title: Variance forecasts benefit more from pooling than complexity
subtitle: 44 next-month realized daily-variance targets • January 2023–August 2026
caption: QLIKE evaluates positive variance forecasts relative to realized central daily variance. The dashed line marks the 63-session persistence benchmark each model must beat. All panels share a scale. MTRN differs from the other issuers: its historical 63-session estimate remains competitive. A lower QLIKE need not also mean lower variance RMSE.

title: MTRN volatility shocks remain difficult to anticipate
subtitle: Square roots of next-month variance targets and variance forecasts • 2023–August 2026
caption: The plotted forecast is sqrt(expected variance), which is not generally expected volatility. No annualization or prediction intervals are applied. Common full-scale axes retain the visible size of missed volatility spikes.

title: Pooling helps risk forecasts more consistently than return forecasts
subtitle: Same 44 targets; individual, all-four and two-company Ridge fits
caption: Return scores use company-specific historical means; variance QLIKE uses the same realized risk target. Pooling uses company indicators and synchronous calendar folds. Business pairs are MTRN/ENTG and CRS/ATI, not asserted homogeneous industries.

title: Correlation is sample-dependent, especially for the recent IPO
subtitle: Daily adjusted-close returns through September 18, 2026 • identical correlation color scale
caption: The long panel has 2,693 shared daily returns; the matched five-equity panel has 102. The right-hand matrix describes only ELMT’s short public sample and is not comparable evidence of long-run diversification. Covariance tables preserve squared-return units separately.

title: Competitor co-movement is not constant
subtitle: MTRN versus ENTG, CRS and ATI • 63-session windows • 2016–September 18, 2026
caption: All pairs use the same daily calendar and correlation scale. Shared changes can weaken diversification when risks rise; the prespecified origin-known volatility-regime comparison is quantified in the accompanying table.
